question.text: Enterprise Value (EV) is best described as:

answer.text: The market capitalisation of a listed company only
The book value per share multiplied by outstanding shares
The value of just the preference shares of a company
The debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business - the value of total capital regardless of whether debt or equity finances it

explanation.text: The Logic: Enterprise Value is the debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business and represents the value of total capital regardless of whether it is financed by debt or equity. The standard bridge is EV = Equity Value + Net Debt + Preference Capital. The Trap: Market capitalisation alone is equity value, not EV. Book value per share multiplied by outstanding shares is the book value of equity. Preference shares alone are only one component of the capital structure. Note: The workbook supports EV as the debt-free, cash-free value of the operating business and provides the EV-to-equity-value bridge.
